light.label: Light
light.summary: The weekly operating system as written, for students in school, college or a job (about 12 to 15 hours a week).

intensive.label: Intensive
intensive.summary: The operating system plus two weak-axis blocks, weekly field missions, extra awareness cards and pitches (about 18 to 22 hours a week).

tasks.title: Choose your programme before you apply
tasks.detail: The 2.5-year M.Des is examined at the same time as the undergraduate programmes, so you can apply for only one. Programme, name, date of birth, mobile number and email cannot be changed later, even in the edit window.

tasks.title: Choose your disciplines and check the combinations
tasks.detail: Apply for one, two or three disciplines. Two: both from the same group (not Group X), or one from Groups 1 to 5 plus one from Group X. Three: two from the same group plus one from Group X. The fee is charged per discipline, and choices cannot be changed later.

tasks.title: Check your eligibility in the 2027-28 handbook
tasks.detail: Read section 5 for the age limits and qualifying-exam rules for your category. Use only the handbook downloaded from admissions.nid.edu.

tasks.title: Diagnostic: score yourself on six axes
tasks.detail: Twenty minutes, honestly. 1 means you have never done this; 5 means you do it reliably under time pressure. Your total sets your band and tunes the plan.

tasks.title: Start your design diary
tasks.detail: One page, four quadrants: what I saw, how it works, where it fails, what I'd change. Ten minutes.

tasks.title: Keep your kit small
tasks.detail: A cheap A4 sketchbook, a 2B pencil, a 0.5 black fineliner, one grey marker and one red pen for annotation.

tasks.title: Set up your critique loop
tasks.detail: Find two other aspirants and fix a weekly exchange day, or join Designforge open critique. Work reviewed within 48 hours teaches.

tasks.title: Prepare your application uploads
tasks.detail: A colour photograph taken at a professional studio and a scanned signature, each a JPG of 50 to 200 KB. Category, PwD or other certificates, where they apply, as PDFs up to 1 MB.

tasks.title: First Sunday review: plan week 1
tasks.detail: Read the four non-negotiables, fix a daily time for your drill, and write down your two lowest diagnostic axes.

tasks.title: Applying to NID Madhya Pradesh or Haryana?
tasks.detail: Their M.Des programmes need a separate application through their own link. Check their websites before 30 November.

tasks.detail: 15 min observation: today's design diary page, this week on ‘Repairs: how Indians fix what breaks’. 20 min: Drawing L5 speed (10 min), then a 60-second explanation of one project (10 min). 10 min: log what broke.

tasks.title: Ten positions and the bank of twenty
tasks.detail: Ten opinions you can hold under disagreement, and twenty things you can talk about for two minutes each.

tasks.title: Awareness index card
tasks.detail: Second card this week. Suggested topic: Craft clusters and the artisan economy.

tasks.title: Sixty-second pitch, recorded
tasks.detail: Context, the problem as you framed it, what you made, what you learned. Mark every filler word and hesitation.

tasks.title: Redo one piece from two weeks ago
tasks.detail: Redo one drawing or concept from two weeks back. The gap between attempts is your evidence of progress.

tasks.title: Daily drill (45 min)
tasks.detail: 15 min observation: today's design diary page, this week on ‘Repairs: how Indians fix what breaks’. 20 min: Drawing L5 speed (10 min), then a 60-second explanation of one project (10 min). 10 min: log what broke.

tasks.title: Full simulation 6: dress rehearsal
tasks.detail: Three hours at the time of day the exam will run. Same kit, same routine.

tasks.title: Review protocol (45 min, same day)
tasks.detail: Score it before you feel anything. Put every error in one bucket: concept, time, clarity or care. Count the buckets, rewrite one answer untimed, and log it in your error ledger.

tasks.title: Sunday review (30 min, written)
tasks.detail: What improved this week, with evidence. What did not move, and why. One change to next week's plan. Tick the week completion check and review your error ledger.

tasks.title: Daily drill, lighter (30 min)
tasks.detail: Diary page and a few loose sketches. Volume down.

tasks.title: Re-read your diary and your position paper
tasks.detail: Notice patterns. Pick five entries you could talk about for two minutes.

tasks.title: Daily drill, lighter (30 min)
tasks.detail: Diary page and a few loose sketches. Volume down.

tasks.title: One short timed studio set (60 min)
tasks.detail: A single brief. No full paper this week.

tasks.title: Daily drill, lighter (30 min)
tasks.detail: Diary page and a few loose sketches. Volume down.

tasks.title: Read your error-ledger patterns
tasks.detail: For each repeating bucket, read the drill that fixes it. No new material.

tasks.title: Daily drill, lighter (30 min)
tasks.detail: Diary page and a few loose sketches. Volume down.

tasks.title: A gentle mock interview (10 min)
tasks.detail: Talk through what is working. Keep it short.

tasks.title: Fix your sleep
tasks.detail: Wake at the time you will need on exam day, and keep it until the 20th.

tasks.title: Daily drill, lighter (30 min)
tasks.detail: Diary page and a few loose sketches. Volume down.

tasks.title: Pack and test your kit
tasks.detail: Admit card printout, photo ID and your drawing kit. Follow any instructions printed on the admit card.

tasks.title: Plan your route to the centre
tasks.detail: Check travel time and leave a buffer before the reporting time on your admit card. NID does not arrange travel or stay.

tasks.detail: Keeps your hand warm without tiring it.
